articleTitle: A downsized and integrated C-band transceiver for VSAT
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We describe a downsized C-band transceiver for VSAT. We have adopted conventional dual frequency conversion and reduced the transceiver size. It integrates four modules, the LNA, down-converter, up-converter, phase-locked LO and high power amplifier (HPA) into one housing. It measures only 245/spl times/170/spl times/145 mm/sup 3/. The LO provides one synthesized output of 4742.5-5242.5 MHz with a step of 500 kHz, and another fixed output of 1112.5 MHz. The HPA outputs more than 3 W over 5925-6425 MHz, and is readily extendible to 5 or 10 Watts. The noise figure of the LNA is less than 40 K. It can operate from -30 /spl deg/C to +70 /spl deg/C and has been continuously in operation for more than eight months.

articleTitle: Statistical estimation of the complex reflection coefficient of microwave loads using a multiport reflectometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new universal technique of microwave network complex reflection coefficient measurement based on the solution of the (N+2)-port equations by the maximum likelihood method is proposed. The expressions for the measurement errors are obtained in a linear approximation. It is shown that the measurement accuracy grows with the increase in the number of measurement ports.

articleTitle: Thermal CAD for power III-V devices and MMICs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A CAD approach (using a hybrid finite-element Green's function strategy) is described for the thermal analysis of GaAs and III-V compound semiconductor devices and integrated circuits. The approach is based on a computationally efficient 3D large-scale thermal simulator allowing for non-linear multilayered and thinned substrates, via holes, and heat conduction through surface metallizations. Simulation examples concerning devices and circuits are discussed to demonstrate the simulator capabilities.

articleTitle: Comprehensive characterization of flip chip contacting methods for microwave and optoelectronic applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Applying state of the art numerical simulation techniques, we have investigated relevant aspects of flip chip contacting methods, which are essential for RF/microwave and optoelectronic applications. An overview of commonly used flip chip mounting methods is given. The electrical properties of flip chip contacts up to millimeter wave frequencies are analyzed. Thermal concepts and mechanical reliability aspects are examined with regard to different bump materials and bump heights. The effect of self-alignment, which is important for optoelectronic devices is explained. Optimization possibilities and design rules are derived. We emphasize the advantages of flip chip technique for RF/microwave and optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis of measurement of complex dielectric permittivity using microstrip transmission line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Microstrip transmission line shows many properties which make it well suited as a medium for complex dielectric permittivity measurement. Such a system could be based on determining the effective permittivity of a microstrip line covered by an unknown dielectric substance. Simple approximate expressions for the effective permittivity are compared with a more rigorous (and hence more computationally involved) solution in order to gain some insight into the accuracy of the approximate solutions with respect to the dielectric material covering the microstrip line. Experimentally determined values of effective permittivity for various standard organic liquids are also presented for comparison.

articleTitle: Mutual impedance of conformal cylindrical microstrip antenna arrays with a protection layer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A model for mutual impedance calculation in probe fed conformal cylindrical microstrip antenna arrays, covered by a protection layer, is presented. The model is based on the Green's function for multilayered cylindrical structures calculated in the Fourier domain. The integral equations for unknown current distributions on the microstrip elements are solved by the method of moments (MOM). As an application, the mutual impedance between two wraparound antennas is calculated.

articleTitle: Short and open circuited slot line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A slot line terminated by the short and open end is analysed by the spectral domain method (SDM). The original process of Yang and Alexopoulos (1988) is modified by application of the piecewise sinusoidal functions only. The reflection coefficient is obtained by fitting the field along the slot described by a superposition of those functions to the standing wave pattern by the least squares method. Closed form formulae of the normalized impedance of the slot line terminated by the short have arisen from fitting its values computed by the SDM. They facilitate CAD of circuits. Full wave analysis of the open-circuited slot line is performed. Agreement between theory and experiment and between our results and data published in the literature is very good.

articleTitle: 1.2 Gb/s SONET/SDH demux in CMOS technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes the design of a demux to meet the requirements of the SONET STS-24 (synchronous transport signal level 24) at a rate of 1.2 Gb/s, using a standard 0.8 /spl mu/m DLM CMOS process. True single phase clocked flip-flops sensitive on both clock edges and deep pipeline techniques are used in order to achieve such a clock rate. The circuit also performs the byte alignment specified in the SONET STS-N frame structure definition.

articleTitle: The photoresponse of microwave HEMTs: semi-analytical modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper is concerned with the response of HEMTs transistors to optical excitation. An experimental evaluation was conducted and a model was developed. The results indicate that the dominant photodetection mechanism is the internal photovoltaic effect (backgating), caused by the accumulation of photogenerated holes in the GaAs buffer layer. Accordingly, the effect of illumination is equivalent to a shift in the gate to source bias point and characterized by a nonlinear photocurrent-optical power relationship. The device exhibits an extremely high quantum efficiency at low optical intensities, but the bandwidth is limited to the MHz range. It is suggested that an additional terminal at the substrate would increase the bandwidth while retaining significant gain over conventional photodiodes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the conductor-backed coplanar waveguide by an alternative formulation of the transverse resonance technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The dispersion characteristics, higher order modes included, of the conductor-backed coplanar waveguide (CBCW) are obtained by an alternative formulation of the transverse resonance technique (TRT). The difference between the usual TRT and the formulation presented here, is the considered transverse equivalent network. With the TRT proposed formulation mode solutions identification requires less arduous work. Numerical results are presented and are in good agreement when compared to results obtained by other methods.

articleTitle: The horizontal structure of rain and its impact on the design of advanced satellite systems at centimetre and millimetre wavelengths
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper deals with the severe propagation problems that will be probably encountered in designing the future satellite communication systems in the Ka band and above and with some possible advanced solutions based on the knowledge of the local climatology. Within the very wide spectrum of new envisaged systems two particularly significant examples have been selected: the TV-sat at 22 GHz and the feeder-links at 20-30 GHz when site diversity configurations will be necessary as expected with low elevation orbiting satellites. As shown in the paper, by exploiting to the maximum extent the available meteorological information, very effective fading and power-saving countermeasures can be envisaged.

articleTitle: An improved model for the GaAs HBT frequency performance under optical illumination
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The theory and model for the GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) frequency performance under optical illumination are described. Photons absorbed in the base-collector depletion region, as well as those absorbed in the neutral base and collector regions are taken into account. The relative importance of these effects and their frequency performance are studied and estimations of the high-frequency photoresponse using PSPICE circuit simulations are shown.

articleTitle: Analysis of normal mode helical antenna on finite ground plane
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The input impedance and the radiation pattern or normal mode helical antenna over a finite size ground plane are investigated. The problem is formulated in terms of the surface integral equation based on the piecewise-sinusoidal reaction concept. The current distribution along the helical wire as well as on the ground plane is determined using the method of moments.

articleTitle: Novel HEMT structures for mixer applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We present two new and original HEMT structures. They have been designed and realized for gate mixer applications. The first HEMT has a decoupling capacitor between the drain and the source. The integrated capacitor acts as a low-pass filter. The second HEMT presents a very nonlinear transconductance profile. The IF signal is provided by the mixing of the RF signal and the second harmonic of the LO signal. Thus, the required LO frequency is divided by 2.

articleTitle: A new semidistributed model for the noise and scattering parameters of the M(H)MIC FETs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes a rigorous and systematic procedure to derive a unified distributed FET (MESFET, HEMT) signal and noise model at centimeter and millimeter-wave frequencies that can easily be implemented in CAD routines of simulators. We have used the three coupled-line theory and for the first time, the experimental data of the device are compared with the full three coupled-line theory and three coupled-line sliced model. The original noise study using the three coupled-line theory is presented. The procedure was used for the complete small-signal characterisation of a submicrometer-gate GaAs NE710 transistor.

articleTitle: A COM model for longitudinally and waveguide coupled SAW resonator filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An extended coupling-of-modes model for longitudinally coupled and for waveguide-coupled surface acoustic wave resonator filters is presented. The relationship between the device structure and performance is examined. Experimental measurements on two 100 MHz devices are used to validate the model.

articleTitle: Green's function approach to the design of SAW filters, containing long unidirectional transducers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Green's function approach (GFA) allows one to evaluate such characteristics of an interdigital transducer (IDT) as the insertion loss and input admittance both in an electrostatic approximation and taking into account surface acoustic waves (SAW) generation. To do this it is necessary to evaluate the charge distribution (CD) along the electrodes of the IDT. This approach makes it possible to evaluate the CD for a single phase unidirectional transducer (SPUDT), having arbitrary types of electrodes (split, floating, nonequidistant etc.). The main disadvantage is the necessity of solving very large (practically more than 500/spl times/500) systems of linear equations for each frequency point, which makes this approach impossible to use for a long SPUDT. A procedure for dramatically reducing the computational time is described. It is based on the evaluation of the CD for a long SPUDT from the CD of a short test transducer. The procedure proposed allows one to determine the insertion loss and impedance of a SPUDT, having arbitrary types of electrodes and arbitrary number of periods, taking into account electrostatic CD and SAW generation. Examples discussed show a good agreement of the approximation proposed with the exact GFA solution.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot intensity modulator for hybrid lidar-radar applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: To improve the detection sensitivity of aerial light detection and ranging (lidar), a hybrid lidar-radar detection scheme has been studied. Preliminary laboratory experiments are promising, but the full-scale realization of this novel system requires the development of high speed modulators for high power, blue-green laser pulses. This paper details experimental and analytical studies performed on a Fabry-Perot modulator suitable for lidar-radar applications.

articleTitle: A low cost MCM-D technology applied to microwave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper presents a new technological solution for fabricating microwave integrated circuits (MICs). This innovative approach is based on a deposited-multichip modules (MCM-D) technology developed at the R&D Centre of TELEBRAS. A description of the processing is presented and some results of MICs fabricated on alumina 96% are shown. The main features of this packaging technology are its low cost (< US$1.5/in/sup 2/), process simplification, reproducibility and microwave devices assembly compatibility. The paper demonstrates an easy solution for MICs fabrication that can be implemented with low investments.

articleTitle: Optical low coherence reflectometry for characterization of optical devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new OLCR configuration, which places the device out of both arms of the Michelson interferometer was demonstrated. By modulating the device-fiber distance the plurality of solutions can be solved. Resolution of 2.5 /spl mu/m and sensitivity of -100 dB enables the system for characterization of optical waveguides.

articleTitle: Green-red light generation and propagation in LiF films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Low energy electron bombardment of LiF polycrystalline films induces an efficient formation of optical active electronic defect emitting in the visible region of the spectrum from green to red at room temperature. A sizeable optical gain coefficient has been measured in the colored region. For the first time light waveguiding has been observed in a LiF film. These result are promising for light generation and propagation in optoelectronic devices based on this interesting material.

articleTitle: Bias unit for microwave and high speed fiber optic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Optoelectronic component interconnections are essential for high data transfer performance in gigabit per second systems and ultrashort pulse applications. Bias "T" units have found extensive use as DC supplies for lasers and photodiodes. However, commercially available units for microwave components operation have not only large dimensions but also very high prices. The very high speed/broadband bias unit presented operates from 100 MHz up to 20 GHz. Thin film technology was used. It was designed for broadband and fast pulse response operation. The measured performance shows good agreement with respect to circuit simulation prediction.

articleTitle: Delayed self homodyne measurements of AM and FM response of modulated multisection diode lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The delayed self homodyne technique was applied to the measurement of the FM response of modulated multisection lasers over a wide frequency range. The AM was observed simultaneously to the FM measurements. A theoretical description of the power spectra measured by the delayed self homodyne is presented. The experimental results using a three section DFB laser are in good agreement with the theoretical model. The distortion of the FM spectrum produced by the IM is also discussed.

articleTitle: A 622.08 MHz narrow bandwidth SAW filter for clock recovery
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes the development of a 622.08 MHz surface acoustic wave (SAW) filter for use in clock recovery units to recover the clock signal from NRZ (non-return-to-zero) data streams in SONET and SDH systems. A narrow bandwidth filter (less than 0.2%) using two different interdigital transducers (IDTs), working on two different harmonic frequencies, was designed and fabricated by the R&D Centre of Telebras. A description of the design and the fabrication are summarized and measurement results of the SAW filter are shown.

articleTitle: Ocean LIDAR technology and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: LIDAR (Light Detection And Ranging) systems have been developed for a wide range of oceanographic applications. This paper first reviews current LIDAR technology and applications. Technology advancements that will enhance the performance level of such systems for underwater investigation in the near future and make their use more economically feasible are then discussed. Transmitter, detector, and filter component improvements will refine the performance of existing systems as well as permit the implementation of new design approaches that take advantage of existing radar signal processing techniques.

articleTitle: Spacecraft antennas-a EUTELSAT perspective
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper reviews the development of linear polarized Ku-band spacecraft antenna technology as seen on the EUTELSAT I and II series of telecommunication satellites and the EUTELSAT Hot Bird series of television broadcast satellites. Some aspects of the design of spacecraft antenna coverages for EUTELSATs are reviewed as well as possible directions for future development of telecommunication spacecraft antennas.

articleTitle: A tridimensional solenoidal basis function to analyze 3D scattering of homogeneous dielectrics using the method of moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The use of rectangular and triangular basis functions with the method of moments to analyze the problem of scattering of electromagnetic waves by dielectric objects with high dielectric constant (/spl epsi//sub I/>10) leads to convergence problems due to the spurious charges associated with the basis functions. This paper proposes a solenoidal 3D basis function that can be used in the method of moments to overcome this problem.

articleTitle: A single six-port reflectometer measures the scattering parameters of two-port microwave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A single six-port reflectometer configuration is proposed to measure the four scattering parameters of two-port microwave devices. In order to determine the transmission coefficients, only one calibration standard and three measurements are required to complete the calibration procedure. Furthermore, s/sub 12/ and s/sub 21/ can be measured without reversing the device under test.

articleTitle: Operation in the TM/sub 10/ mode of a microstrip antenna on a conical surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A theoretical development is presented for the analysis of microstrip antennas on conical surfaces, operating in the TM/sub 10/ mode. The cavity model with magnetic side walls is used for the calculation of the resonant frequency and input impedance. The dyadic Green's function formulation is used to calculate the radiated fields and the radiation quality factor. Particular antennas me examined and numerical results for operation in the TM/sub 10/ mode are shown.

articleTitle: Heterojunction bipolar transistors under illumination: theory and experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new model for the HBT has been developed which solves for the electrical and photogenerated currents in the base, emitter, and collector. The model accounts for the discontinuity in the quasi-fermi level by defining an effective carrier interface velocity. Experimental and theoretical curves relating to the device behavior are presented and compared.

articleTitle: A 2.488 Gb/s GaAs 1:4/1:16 demultiplexer IC with skip circuit for SONET STS-12/48 systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A 1:4/1:16 demultiplexer IC with an integrated skip circuit has been successfully designed and fabricated employing SCFL standard cells based on 1 /spl mu/m MESFET foundry technology. The circuit was designed to operate at up to 2.5 Gb/s with low power dissipation. The demultiplexer employs a tree type architecture based on 1:2 demux blocks using tristage flip-flops. A new skip circuit without re-timing was proposed and integrated in the demultiplexer for frame alignment. The proposed skip circuit demonstrated its effectiveness and the IC operated either as a 1:4 or a 1:16 demultiplexer at up to 2.5 Gb/s with a power dissipation of 1 W. This IC is applicable for signal processing on SONET STS-12/48 optical communication systems.

articleTitle: The applications of photonics to radar: a system designer's perspective
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A generic active array radar system is defined, and a brief functional description of the subsystems presented. For comparison, two contemporary conceptual views of optically controlled arrays are discussed, and the transition to a more realistic architecture model is described. Several proposed photonic antenna systems from the current literature are critiqued with respect to the model.

articleTitle: Carrier recombination in single and double heterojunction bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Carrier recombination in single and double abrupt bipolar transistors (HBTs) is analysed. The numerical results performed on InP based structures show that the recombination rate in the neutral base of double abrupt HBTs is higher than in single abrupt HBTs owing to the electron confinement in the base region.

articleTitle: Frequency selective fade effects and bandwidth considerations in COST 235
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Working Group 1 in the COST 235 Project study frequency selective effects and their impact on digital radio links. For fixed communication links the trend for many years has been of increasing the capacity without necessarily a larger bandwidth, e.g., 155 Mbit/s or 622 Mbit/s links in the synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) network. This lead to complex techniques that are more sensitive to distortion caused by propagation as well as other sources. The techniques used to achieve a greater transmission capacity are higher levels of modulation by combining more bits into a single symbol and by use of dual polarisation. The multipath mitigation techniques cover various diversity reception schemes, transmit power control, channel equalisers, and error correction coding. A deeper understanding of multipath propagation mechanisms is needed both for the development of the various prediction techniques as well as the development of equipment. The Working Group has compiled a database for testing purposes of existing and new prediction methods. It has been of particular importance to include measurements of performance, e.g. bit error rates (BER), as part of the data to be able to give recommendations regarding the merits of various prediction methods.

articleTitle: Site shielding and other interference reduction strategies in COST 235
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper presents topic areas in the form of ten questions formulated at the start of COST Project 235 which have been investigated by Working Group 3. Many of the problems identified have received in-depth studies analytically and experimentally. The paper outlines the significant progress achieved in the formulation of a generalised site shielding procedure and more generally in the modelling of urban radiowave propagation for use in radio system planning and coordination.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field studies in urban environment with a higher-order parabolic equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The study of the field distribution, when a small-cellular environment is considered, requires models that are able to take into account the effects of diffraction and backscattering due to the presence of nearby buildings. This has led to further developments of the parabolic equation techniques. In this paper a 2-D model that makes use of a wide-angle parabolic equation is described, a domain decomposition is applied and transparent boundary conditions are used on the upper boundary to simulate the radiation condition.

articleTitle: Marconi and the invention of wireless communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In the author's opinion, Radio, intended as the possibility of transmitting information over long distance through free electromagnetic waves, was a long and difficult parturition, which began in the spring of 1895 with the first experiments of Pontecchio, and ended in 1901, at Signal Hill, at St. John's, Newfoundland, with the first transatlantic transmission. In fact, if the activity Marconi carried out between 1896 and 1901 hadn't been successful, the experiments of the year 1895 would have just opened the way to the invention of Radio, because, as the author notes later, the instruments were not yet syntonic, while the ionosphere had not been discovered yet. The latter had a fundamental role in very-long-distance communications, in particular in the intercontinental communications, until the age of the communications via satellite. As a conisequence, speaking of the invention of Radio is equivalent to speak of the whole period above-mentioned, and not of a single event. The author goes into details in what is significant from a technical point of view in the period going from the autumn of 1894 to December 1901.

articleTitle: The mutual coupling effect on the input impedance and radiation pattern of Yagi antenna in an array environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The classical dipole theory has been extended to determine the mutual coupling effect on the parameters of the Yagi-Uda antenna in the array environment. The approach is very simple and useful in designing a Yagi antenna array and takes a shorter computer time as compared to the commonly used numerical technique of the method of moments. Experiments which were carried out to validate the theoretical results, show very good agreement.

articleTitle: Background to COST Project 235 [MM wave radio propagation]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Three European COST Projects have successfully stimulated research on topical concerns on tropospheric radiowave propagation. These have led to reports and expertise relevant to system planning in Europe and to world-wide planning through contributions to ITU-R (and previously CCIR). Currently, a fourth, COST Project 235, has been investigating constraints and opportunities for radiowave propagation on future digital and millimetre-wave systems, primarily for fixed terrestrial systems. It has been examining effects of frequency-selective fading (e.g. due to multipath propagation) and due to non-frequency-selective fading (e.g. due to atmospheric gases, precipitation and scintillation), and site shielding and other interference reduction strategies. Two interim reports have been produced. The project is essentially committed to meeting user requirements. Mention is also made of a future planned project.

articleTitle: A simple method for the chirp reduction in single-frequency semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The direct current modulation of single-longitudinal mode semiconductor lasers causes a dynamic shift of the peak emission wavelength (chirping) arising from gain-induced variations of the laser refractive index. This linewidth broadening results in data-dependent distortion in long-haul, high-bit-rate, direct detection optical communication systems due to interaction with the generally nonzero chromatic dispersion of monomode fibers. Here it is shown that the frequency chirping of 1.55 /spl mu/m DFB lasers and the bit error of the system can be greatly reduced by the use of a delta stub in the microstrip driving circuit of the laser.

articleTitle: Flat-fade effects and millimetre-wave considerations in COST 235
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes some of the activities of Working Group 2 of COST Project 235 on radiowave propagation effects on next-generation fixed-services terrestrial telecommunications systems. Working Group 2 is concerned with the "flat-fade" effects on such systems, including absorption and dispersion by atmospheric gases, attenuation and scattering by hydrometeors, especially by rain and the effects of atmospheric turbulence manifested in scintillation phenomena.

articleTitle: Jaggedness free C-OFDR for optical components characterization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: High resolution and high sensitivity optical components characterization was performed with a jaggedness free coherent optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR) with multi-electrode DFB laser. The fading noise was reduced to less than 1 dB by using a double optical frequency sweep, improving the accuracy of insertion loss measurements. Sensitivities down to -105 dB were achieved with minute measurement times.

articleTitle: Thermal-time response measurement of a distributed feedback laser using coherent reflectometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The thermal behavior of distributed feedback semiconductor lasers, with two different structures, was investigated by using a coherent reflectometry system. The thermal-time responses were estimated for step modulated laser operation and it was possible to analyze the influence of the package on the total response, this is an important limitation in the linearity of optical frequency sweep in optical frequency domain reflectometry. The influence of the amplitude and frequency modulation was also investigated.

articleTitle: Prediction of optimum large-signal microwave MESFET efficiency in multiplication and power amplification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A method is described which enables the optimum large-signal efficiency to be obtained for a microwave active device independently of the required nonlinear function. The technique consists of determining the volume surrounded by a surface called the "characteristic surface" including all the allowed powers at the terminal ports of the nonlinear component in order to deduce its optimum "intrinsic" powers and then its corresponding optimum efficiency. Applied to MESFETs, the design of both a frequency multiplier and a power amplifier permits one to validate this method.

articleTitle: A new optical source for generation of 40-60 GHz signals using a dual mode multisection DFB semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new optical source for generation of pure and high power millimetre-wave signals between 40-60 GHz using a dual mode multisection semiconductor laser is demonstrated. Phase-locked millimetre-waves are generated with extremely narrow linewidth (<10 Hz) and wide locking range (/spl sim/500 MHz).

articleTitle: Influence of Cl doping in the optical and electrical properties of ZnSe grown by molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Using ZnCl/sub 2/ as a doping source, we have grown epitaxial layers of Cl-doped ZnSe onto GaAs substrates by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). The maximum carrier concentration obtained was 1.2 10/sup 19/ cm/sup -3/. An increase in the deep level emission was observed in the photoluminescence (PL) spectra of highly doped samples. By deep level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) measurements four electron traps with energy levels of Ec=0.50, 0.68, 0.74 and 1.20 eV were detected.

articleTitle: A finite element-boundary integral analysis of electromagnetic scattering by a buried dielectric object
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The application of a hybrid finite element-boundary integral (FE-BI) technique to the scattering from a dielectric cylinder buried in a dielectric half-space is presented. The domain in which FEM has to be applied is limited by a fictitious surface /spl Gamma/. The scattered field distribution is numerically evaluated by imposing the proper boundary conditions at the surface /spl Gamma/ and by using a suitable Green's function representation which allows one to take into account the presence of the interface.

articleTitle: A new and efficient approach to the accurate simulation of phase noise in microwave MESFET oscillators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We present a new and efficient approach to the simulation of accurate near-carrier phase noise in free-running microwave MESFET oscillators. First, a new kind of noise analysis model of the oscillators is proposed that contains a complete nonlinear noise model of the MESFET. Then an efficient algorithm is proposed to predict the accurate near-carrier phase noise in the microwave MESFET oscillators by the nonlinear current method. Examples of application prove that the new approach is suitable for microwave CAD and excellent in both efficiency and precision in predicting phase noise in the microwave MESFET oscillators.

articleTitle: Near field solutions for chirostrip printed dipoles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Numerical solutions for near electromagnetic fields excited by short dipoles printed on grounded chiral slabs are presented. Using the full-wave spectral-domain analysis method developed for open chirostrip structures, expressions for electromagnetic field components are obtained. The effects of chirality on the near field distributions and on the dispersion curves of the surface wave modes are discussed. The results of this investigation confirm that all guided modes are hybrid and that bifurcated modes, currently observed in other chirowaveguide structures, are absent in grounded chiral slabs.

articleTitle: Microwave phase conjugation using arrays of nonlinear optically pumped devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Phase conjugation is a technique for reversing both the direction of propagation and the overall phase factor of an incoming wave. Up to date, most developments have concentrated on the optical regime due to the availability of nonlinear materials and power density restrictions. The extension of phase conjugation techniques to microwave frequencies has been explored using mixing elements with antennas [Cutler et al., 1963]. In this work, we report the use of optical signals as carriers of the microwave pump signal. This optical injection technique is the key to making simple, viable, low cost microwave phase conjugation arrays and nonlinear microwave surfaces.

articleTitle: Distortion in a semiconductor laser under quasi-sinusoidal current modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Both intensity modulation (IM) and frequency modulation (FM) of a directly-modulated semiconductor laser are considered. Harmonic and intermodulation distortions are evaluated with the aid of a nonlinear differential equation for the photon density. Theoretical results are obtained through the Bessel function and the perturbation methods. They allow one to compare FM and IM distortion levels, as well as the two calculation methods.

articleTitle: MMIC and fiber optic delay line hybrid transversal filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Microwave transversal filters suffer from bandwidth limitations and the inability to provide long time delays due to losses and dispersion in the microstrip delay line. Purely optical transversal filter disadvantages include inaccurate weighting and the inability to provide negative weighting coefficients. Therefore, a novel hybrid transversal filter configuration that utilizes the optical fiber as a delay mechanism, with negligible loss and wide bandwidth, and an existing monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) transversal filter to provide the necessary accurate positive and negative weighting is presented. The noise performance, dispersion due to the delay line, and a comparison of frequency responses of the existing MMIC advanced transversal filter, the hybrid transversal filter and an ideal filter are reported. The optimum hybrid filter configuration is determined from an analysis of various configurations.

articleTitle: Analysis of E-plane discontinuities of bilateral metal septa with finite conductivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The equivalent lossy T-network parameters of E-plane discontinuities (in rectangular waveguides) of bilateral metal septa with finite conductivity are calculated by the method of lines. An efficient approach is presented to extend this numerical method to EM boundary value problems with imperfectly conducting metal boundaries parallel to the discretization lines. Numerical results of both equivalent reactances and resistances in the T-network are obtained. The calculated insertion losses of a Ka-band filter based on the lossy equivalent circuit fit better with the published experimental results than what have been obtained based on a lossless equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: A low power consumption GaAs MMIC transimpedance amplifier for 2.5 Gb/s optical receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper presents a GaAs MMIC transimpedance amplifier for a high bit rate (2.5 Gb/s) optical communication system. A GaAs integrated circuit with a transimpedance gain of 63 dBohm, a bandwidth of 1.8 GHz with high capacitance photodiode operation and low power consumption is demonstrated. A complete set of simulated and measured results are presented to confirm the effectiveness of the design approach. The circuit design was carried out at R&D Center of TELEBRAS together with University of Rome through the ITU/UNDP project and the prototypes were fabricated at GEC-Marconi.

articleTitle: Comparative performance of the reduced integration penalty approach for removing spurious FE solutions of dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The reduced integration penalty method and the use of vector interpolation are two basically different new approaches for eliminating spurious finite element solutions of dielectric waveguides. Their computational performances are compared in terms of the convergence of the eigenvalues considering the mesh densities, computation times and storage demands, and highlighting their significant features.

articleTitle: MEF system: an object-oriented finite element package
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The article presents a generic finite element package which solves a great number of electromagnetic and related problems. The adoption of object-oriented programming for the software implementation allows the treatment of complex problems and the use of the existent code for the solution of new formulations.

articleTitle: Radiometric measurements of the effective rain height in the tropics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents results of an investigation of the quasi-instantaneous and statistical behaviour of the effective rain height for rain attenuation (at 12 GHz) in satellite links. The results are derived from point rainfall rate and radiometric attenuation measurements at two sites in the tropical and equatorial regions of Brazil.

articleTitle: Optimizing integrated-optics polarizers for maximum polarization isolation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Available technologies currently permit the construction of optical integrated polarizers employing accurate features with dimensions considerably smaller than the operation wavelength. These devices may have a relatively small number of grooves and rely on the wave-polarization dependence of the groove scattering to achieve their results. To achieve optimum performance (e.g., maximum polarization isolation) they must be modeled with an accuracy only possible through the use of rigorous vector diffraction theory. One such technique is applied to analyze and design perfectly conducting polarizers with finite number of arbitrarily-shaped features. The currents flowing on the grooves' surfaces are rigorously obtained, and from them the scattered field is determined. As an application example, the dimensions of the first and last grooves of a 20-triangular-grooves polarizer, operating at 1 /spl mu/m wavelength, are optimized to yield a polarization isolation of 57 dB.

articleTitle: Narrowband solid state acousto-optic tunable filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper reveals a unique design for a narrowband tunable optical filter employing acousto-optic technology. The filter provides tuning capability over the entire blue-green spectral region within one second. The design configuration offers maximum economy, remarkable versatility, uniform spectral response and constant narrow bandwidth less than 0.3 nm. The proposed filter architecture uses state-of-the art technology and components to meet the tuning speed and resolution requirements.

articleTitle: On null steering in rectangular planar array using external elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Two methods of null steering in planar arrays are described. One utilizes four external elements oriented along the symmetrical axes of the array and the other uses two of the actual edge elements of the array together with two external elements placed beyond the other ends of the array. In both methods the choice of the external element positions and the use of conjugated phase shifts are utilized to produce a superimposed interferometer pattern whose peaks coincide, approximately, with all of the peaks of the sidelobes and whose zeros coincide with the nulls of the array pattern. Simple closed form expressions for the amplitudes of the cancellation signals that fed to the external elements are given. A comparison is made between the two methods.

articleTitle: Effect of tunneling current on the modeling of AlGaAs/GaAs and InP/InGaAs/InP HBTs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: HBTs of AlGaAs/GaAs and InP/InGaAs are characterized and modeled. The effect of the tunneling current through the spike at the emitter-base heterojunction is analysed and shown that it is possible to include it in the Ebers-Moll model. A comparison of the measured current of the HBTs with the current calculated by the modified Ebers-Moll model, which includes the thermionic emission, is presented.

articleTitle: Differential rain attenuation in converging links
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents results of differential attenuation measurements in 6 terrestrial line-of-sight microwave links with a common end at Sao Paulo, in the tropical region of Brazil. One link operates at 18 GHz and five links at 15 GHz. An empirical method used to estimate the differential attenuation exceeded at a given percentage of time as a function of the angle between links and their path length difference was developed based on the experimental results.

articleTitle: An improved model to design integrated optical pressure sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An improved model for the design of multilayered diaphragm type integrated optical pressure sensors is reported. In this new model the multilayered diaphragm structure is based on an equivalent single-layer which is simulated by using the finite-difference method (FDM). Numerical results of the halfwave pressure as a function of the diaphragm length show good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: S band compact antennas on handsets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new type of small broadband antennas easily integrated on handsets is presented. Their integration on handsets can be very easy. Designed for transmission or reception in the S band (1885/2025 MHz (transmit band) and 2110/2200 MHz (receive band)), where new services will be soon available, these antennas are inserted on handsets simulated by metallic boxes. Their characterization (return loss and far field patterns) are given, taking into account the hand-held telephone isolated in space. Compact circular antennas have been developed for satellite mobile links.

articleTitle: Characterization of RF/microwave packaging structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Various RF/microwave packaging structures are investigated by a numerical full wave analysis. In frequency ranges up to 80 GHz chip contacting methods are characterized. Coplanar waveguide-to-coax and -to-microstrip and coax-to-microstrip transitions are treated. Optimization and sensitivity curves are given. The simulation results can be used for introducing some standard RF/microwave packaging structures.

articleTitle: Synthesis of optimum radiolocation complexes of remote probing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper considers the interaction of active and passive radiolocation systems working jointly. The receiver device synthesis is via Markov's theory of nonlinear optimal filtering. Both the radiometer and radar use signal polarizable processing. A four channel receiver architecture and an equation for the information parameter measurement estimation variance are obtained a result of the synthesis. A comparison of the measurement error of the integrated system and its separate elements showed that the error in the first case is always lower than in the second. This advantage is more significant under a low signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: ASK/PSK Modulator in Planar Structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference

articleTitle: Novel electronically tunable DR band-stop filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes the fundamental characteristics and experimental results of a newly developed electronically tunable dielectric resonator (DR) band-stop filter. The tuning configuration employed consists of a microstrip line ring loaded with GaAs varactor diodes. The tuning circuit has been developed to produce large variation in the dielectric resonator's fundamental TE/sub 01/spl delta// mode resonant frequency without affecting its quality factor significantly. The 4-pole filter fabricated is compact and light weight, exhibiting a tuning bandwidth of 58 MHz with steep attenuation slope.

articleTitle: Some nonlinear integrated optical devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Nonlinear integrated optical devices have been widely investigated in the last decade due to the possibility of realising all optical devices. Two classes of nonlinear devices are discussed: directional couplers as spatial filtering and as wavelength filtering devices, and spatial selection of the beam, by the help of spatial soliton interaction in the waveguide. These devices are analyzed assuming a third order nonlinear material. A discussion of the cubic behaviour of a second order nonlinear material is also included, considering in particular the wavelength filtering properties of the directional coupler.

articleTitle: Discriminator using a dual-mode dielectric-resonator-loaded cavity for narrowband microwave receiver applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An original dielectric resonator dual-mode discriminator is described for narrow band low-cost microwave receiver applications. The device is useful for receivers possessing an ultimate bandwidth from 5 to 50 MHz. An application is presented where the discriminator is used for automatic frequency control in a Ku-band satellite beacon receiver.

articleTitle: Phase dispersion characterization of fibre gratings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A high wavelength resolution set-up based on an interferometric technique has been used to provide accurate phase dispersion and time delay measurements of fibre photorefractive gratings. Standard and highly chirped gratings has been characterized and the results used to develop a chirped fibre filter which can be used for dispersion-compensation in long fibre telecommunications links, thus greatly enhancing the capacity of the existing fibre base.

articleTitle: Class AB power amplifier advanced design techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Relevant existing design procedures for microwave class-AB power amplifiers are briefly reviewed and discussed, focusing on their field of application and relative strength or drawbacks. Both simplified and accurate nonlinear methodologies are addressed.

articleTitle: Diffractive structures in integrated optics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Integrated optical diffractive structures can be profitably used in a variety of applications. Grating couplers, for example, are suitable for waveguide characterization, while more complex components, such as Fresnel lenses, can constitute the focusing elements of most IO signal processing devices. We consider both practical and design aspects of the realization of several waveguide diffractive structures, namely the implementation of a fabrication process of gratings in glass substrates, and the design optimization of various types of Fresnel lenses.

articleTitle: Quasi-static model for circular transmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Models have been developed for circular transitions of commonly used transmission lines, such as the stripline and the microstrip line, and have been included in commercial microwave CAD packages. Yet no general theory has been made for modeling the bends of other transmission lines, such as the coplanar waveguide. A model was derived for general circular transmission lines, based on a quasi-static approximation. This model was applied to a circular coplanar waveguide. Measurement of the latter showed good agreement with the model.

articleTitle: Accurate evaluation of the electric fields generated for microwave hyperthermia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The article presents original formulations of the E-fields generated by a vertical dipole immersed in a dissipative medium. From the latter the E-fields generated by a vertical interstitial antenna in the surrounding medium can be descended with almost analytic accuracy. This allows fast evaluation of the injected power distributions versus frequency, medium parameters and antenna geometry. The result is of major interest in applications such as the microwave hyperthermia that is a reliable technique in the therapy of localised tumours.

articleTitle: Fullwave analysis of coplanar asymmetrical stripline, with application in guided-wave optical devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The method of lines (MoL) is employed for a fullwave analysis of the propagation characteristics of lossless, coplanar asymmetrical striplines, considering conductor-backed and suspended substrate configurations. The variation of the effective dielectric constant and characteristic impedance with frequency and dimensions is investigated. The results obtained find application in guided-wave optical devices.

articleTitle: Optimization of a MESFET RF power amplifier using a bias dependent large signal MESFET model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A large signal quasistatic MESFET model with bias dependent elements is derived from both experimental S parameters and DC measurements. As an application, this model is used in the design of a MESFET power amplifier. The analysis and gain optimization of the amplifier is performed using the describing function technique. Maximum gain is obtained by the determination of the optimum bias device conditions. The experimental results show excellent agreement with the CAD simulation.

articleTitle: Pro's and con's of TDMA and CDMA for digital cellular networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The main differences of today's TDMA (the GSM system family) and CDMA systems (the IS-95 CDMA) and their relative performance are shown. Technical features like frequency hopping, hand-off, hierarchical cell structures, power control, voice activity detection, equalization and RAKE reception are discussed. The speech coder is shown as the most essential part of a system in terms of quality and capacity. A comparison between the two systems is made for the important parameters of range and capacity from the network operators point of view.

articleTitle: Dielectric and magnetic anisotropy effect on the nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide dispersion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The combined effect of dielectric and magnetic anisotropy in NRD waveguides is investigated. The analysis shows how these media characteristics affects the propagation of modes corresponding to the fundamental LSM and LSE modes. Numerical results are presented for some common materials like sapphire, Epsilam-10, PTFE and glass. An accurate knowledge of this dispersion is important for the design and analysis of NRD devices at millimeter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Active microstrip array for satellite communication applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In this paper two microstrip arrays designed manufactured and tested for the needs of DBS signal reception in the X-band are presented. The TPA-256 antenna was a passive array and the TPA-256A antenna was an active one. TPA-256 and TPA-256A differed in their beamforming networks (BFN)-BFN of the TPA-256A array contained two microwave low noise amplifiers (LNA) to increase antenna sensitivity. The contribution includes theoretical and experimental results. Consideration is also given to reduction of a feeding network spurious radiation in microstrip arrays.

articleTitle: New method for the numerical analysis of the quasi-optical resonators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We investigate an alternative method of the numerical analysis of the quasi-optical resonator modes. The resonator is viewed as a waveguide transverse to its axis. The fields of the resonator modes are expanded in the form of the guide modes, which are coupled by the change of the waveguide cross section, the mirrors edges, etc. The amplitudes of the modes are derived from a system of ordinary differential equations. The boundary conditions for the amplitudes are obtained by the generalized scattering matrices method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Volterra processor for fringe order identification in white-light interferometric systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Comparatively high success rates with the application of linear adaptive least mean square (LMS) algorithms to identify the zero order fringe in the presence of additive Gaussian noise only have been reported in spatially-scanned white-light interferometric (WLI) systems. However, when the corrupting noise causing the problems with fringe identification is signal-dependent and/or exhibits transient behaviour mainly attributable to mechanical vibrations (shocks) in such systems, nonlinear filtering accompanied by a suitable adaptation algorithm should lead to better overall performance. The paper presents a study conducted to appraise the use of Volterra processors in conjunction with adaptive LMS, against the linear filtering counterpart previously published, when the analogue-to-digital (A/D) converters employed in the interferometric system introduce quadratic and/or cubic nonlinearity distortion. The paper also attempts to resolve the linear/nonlinear modelling dilemma of a suspected kind of nonlinearity due to chromatic aberration effects which manifests two important characteristics in the fringe pattern, namely, skewness and nonGaussianity. It is shown that the Volterra processor produces less satisfactory results than a linear filter with optimal choice of the step size parameter. Thus contradicting the hypothesis which regards the effects of chromatic aberrations as nonlinear.

articleTitle: Distortion and coupling analysis of short electric pulses on lossy, coupled microstrip lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The propagation characteristics of short electric pulses on lossy, coupled microstrip lines is thoroughly investigated using full wave methods. It is shown that mode coupling is the main cause of pulse distortion, and that it can be controlled by appropriate choice of the substrate composition. The results obtained indicate the feasibility of VLSI circuits with high conductor density, keeping the crosstalk and distortion due to mode coupling under control.

articleTitle: Wide flare angle Ku band axially corrugated horn for offset VSAT antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A wide semi-flare angle linearly tapered corrugated horn, with eight axial slots, has been developed for use in single offset antennas for VSAT earth stations with low cross-polarization peak levels from 10.7 GHz to 14.8 GHz. Mode-matching techniques have been successfully applied to the horn return loss and radiation pattern prediction and the critical effects of the ridges and output flange thicknesses have been verified.

articleTitle: Optical power budget allocation in linear embedding and active delimitation electro-optic router network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The design of an optical fiber network with linear embedding and active delimitation electro-optic router (LEADER), based on an array of optical amplifiers is presented. An analytical theory is used with prediction of the spontaneous noise power influence. The power budget allocation in the network can be calculated using the results. The longitudinal dependence of the photon population in the active region of the semiconductor optical amplifier is considered.

articleTitle: Nonlinear propagation in an optical fractal structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We study the nonlinear propagation and the spatial distribution of a TE field in an integrated structure realized by alternating two dielectric layers of different Kerr-type nonlinear materials, whose refractive index is such that the highest refractive layers belong to a Canter set.

articleTitle: Optimized power performance of tunable fiber ring lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The optimized power performance of tunable fiber ring lasers governed by two-level rate equations is presented. A figure of merit and an optimization procedure are defined in order to obtain maximum output power for a given pump power. A tunable Er-doped fiber ring laser was assembled as an example. Experimental data and theoretical predictions are compared.

articleTitle: A hybrid method solution of scattering by conducting cylinders (TM case)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The finite element or finite difference techniques are well known for the solution of Maxwell's equation in the differential form. But terminating the mesh accurately at a finite distance from the body in the case of an open problem is a major challenge. The method of Sadiku (see Numerical Techniques in Electromagnetics, CRC Press, Inc., Boca Raton, 1992) is applied for only the electrostatic problem. This hybrid method is applied for the TM scattering problem and the results are documented in this paper. This new approach, as in the electrostatic case, allows for the terminating surface to encapsulate the body very tightly. As before, the finite element technique is used for open region problems whereas the integral equation solution approach using Green's function is applied to enforce the radiation condition. At each iteration cycle, the induced currents on the conducting cylinder are evaluated and their scattered field at the terminating surface is calculated. Using this method for the TM case, the computational efficiency of the finite element method can be increased. It can be generalized for the case of inhomogeneous and nonlinear media, for static and dynamic fields. Numerical results are presented for the solution of Helmholtz's equation to illustrate the accuracy of the technique.

articleTitle: GaAs Fabry-Perot modulator for microwave applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A distributed bragg reflector Fabry-Perot modulator for microwave applications is considered. The device consists of a Fabry-Perot cavity formed by etching gratings on a rib waveguide with a buried GaAs guiding layer. Computer simulations based on the finite difference method were used to model the device. State-of-the-art first order gratings with a pitch of 0.20 /spl mu/m have been successfully fabricated.

articleTitle: 10 Gbit/s byte-interleaver and de-interleaver with silicon ICs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: For an experimental STM-64 system two very fast silicon MSI circuits were developed and fabricated, which make it possible to multiplex and demultiplex in a byte-by-byte mode up to 10 Gbit/s. To obtain a 4:1 multiplexing (resp. a 1:4 demultiplexing) three identical multiplexer- (resp. demultiplexer-) chips are necessary. Due to economical reasons three of the four channels are filled in the described system with pseudorandom signals.

articleTitle: Operation of a 32 GHz pulsed gyrotron
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The design and operation of a high power pulsed gyrotron are reported. The device runs in pulsed regime with a 25 /spl mu/s pulse length at a frequency repetition rate of 10 Hz and during operation the pressure in the tube is ordinarily less than 4.0/spl times/10/sup -7/ Torr. Several TE modes were detected over the magnetic field range 9.5 to 12.5 kG and the measured resonant frequencies (29.0 to 32.0 GHz) showed to be in close agreement with the self-consistent calculated values. Experiments are currently under way to measure the absolute ouput power and to identify the modes through field pattern measurement techniques.

articleTitle: Trade-off performance properties of pHEMT-based LNAs vs. temperature for VSAT applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The optimum trade-off performance of an LNA for VSAT applications based on a commercial pHEMT series have been investigated vs. temperature, starting from a noisy model fitted to the measured devices's scattering parameters and noise figure values. As a result, it has been noted that with decreasing temperature from room value, the combined minimum noise figure-power gain (Fmin-Gass), reported on the microwave low-noise device's data sheets, doesn't represent a useful working condition for an optimum LNA design.

articleTitle: Modeling of scattering by particle on layered substrate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Light scattering by a penetrable particle at the surface of a layered substrate is investigated. The complete mathematical model is analyzed using the method of discrete sources. The results of the investigation are compared with the numerical and experimental data.

articleTitle: Improving holographic storage in LiNbO/sub 3/ crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We show that the use of actively stabilized holographic recording improves the performance of LiNbO/sub 3/ photorefractive crystals as optical storage media. Reproducible and highly efficient holograms are obtained in this way, even in the presence of rather weak recording beams and low modulated images. Experimental results are reported using an Fe-doped crystal and a 514.5 nm wavelength illumination.

articleTitle: High temperature superconducting microstrip resonators for the measurement of films made by pyrolysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Microwave surface impedance measurements are reported for textured granular YBCO films made by a novel spray pyrolysis method on the surface of a YSZ substrate. A parallel plate resonator was formed by placing the film and substrate on top of a copper ground plane. Microwave measurements were made at nitrogen temperatures on the fundamental mode at /spl sim/4.7 GHz. A model has been developed to extract the penetration depth and impedance of the finite thickness granular film. We obtain values for penetration depth /spl lambda//sub g//spl sim/3.6 /spl mu/m and, using independent measurements of the critical current and grain size, a surface resistance R/sub g//spl sim/13 m/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: Backscattering synthesis from tapered resistive grids
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes how to synthesize a tapered resistive grid that produces a desired backscattering pattern. The grid consists of equally spaced, equal width strips. Each strip has a resistivity that is found by using a genetic algorithm. Physical optics is used to calculate the backscattering. The results are compared with the method of moments calculations.

articleTitle: EM wave propagation in a Cantor-like corrugated waveguide geometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The spectral transmission properties of a self-similar corrugated optical waveguide are theoretically studied. The considered structure can be realized by a planar waveguide with a square wave modulation of the guiding film thickness such that the thickest layers belong to a triadic Cantor set. The transmission spectrum exhibits localized peaks inside forbidden frequency band gaps. This feature could be very useful in the design of novel filters. The nonlinear behaviour of the structure is also considered.

articleTitle: Improvements in the waveform relaxation method applied to transmission lines with nonlinear terminations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The waveform relaxation algorithm proposed by Chang (1990) applying to the transient analysis of coupled transmission lines has been found to have a problem in dealing with the DC components of the solution waveforms. This paper applies the modified waveform relaxation algorithms to the simulation of lossy coupled lines with nonlinear terminations. The results are compared with those generated by the conventional time-stepping method.

articleTitle: Techniques to increase the spectrum efficiency of high capacity digital radios
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents the research on digital radio communications designed to increase the transmission capacity, i.e., spectral efficiency (bits/s/Hz), as well as the necessary requirements and limitations imposed by these systems. An overview of this evolution, which led to an efficient high capacity transmission is presented and some countermeasures and transmission techniques, like frequency reuse, are also analyzed. Performance results, evaluated at Vimercate (Milan) and in some experimental links in Italy, demonstrating the improvements of these techniques are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A spectral domain method for multiple scattering in transition layer of two-scale random surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The spectral domain method is extended to a wavefield propagating in the transition layer of a two-scale random surface. The integral equations set for the two-dimensional Fourier spectra of the wavefield by scattering from the random surface is obtained: the shadow and multiple scattering effects are taken into account in the approach. The solution of this set can be computed by a number of iterations.

articleTitle: The six-port reflectometer: choosing a calibration method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents a discussion on four known and frequently employed six-port reflectometer calibration procedures, namely the ones by Glenn Engen (1978), Ghannouchi et al. (1988), Sunil Judah (1985) and Cong-Zhen Qian (1985). The desired features usually sought in a calibration method, like accuracy, ease of calibration and low cost, among others, are discussed for each method above. The procedure introduced by Engen can lead to the determination of the scattering parameters of microwave devices from power measurements only, without the complex circuitry of the heterodyne network analyzer.

articleTitle: CAD for the synthesis of rectangular microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: There are many powerful CAD-packages for the analysis of microstrip antennas. But the literature hasn't reported any CAD-package for the synthesis of this type of antenna. A PC software for the synthesis of coaxially fed rectangular microstrip antennas is presented, using the improved transmission line method to predict the input characteristics of a rectangular microstrip antenna. Results are shown in which there is good agreement between the synthesis and experimental results obtained by other authors.

articleTitle: Suspended microstrip patch resonators on magnetized ferrites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Lately, a growing interest in the development of microstrip antennas on magnetized ferrites has been observed, because they offer magnetic tuning and scanning capabilities. A suspended microstrip patch resonator on a magnetized ferrite offers another tuning possibility, which is obtained by varying the distance from the ground plane to the ferrimagnetic layer. The authors investigate the tuning capability of suspended microstrip patch resonators by using a combination of the Hertz potentials and the moment methods. Curves of the resonant frequency and the Q factor are presented as functions of the suspended microstrip patch resonator geometry.

articleTitle: Selected topics on the analysis and fabrication of high-frequency MMICs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the main issues affecting the design, fabrication and testing of monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs). After a discussion of contemporary CAD techniques the benefits of modern manufacturing techniques are outlined and customer driven applications are described.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of the electric field and potential of multiwire electrodes in X-ray detectors by the method of moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A software package for treating electrostatic phenomena in the active medium of an X-ray detector is presented. Use is made of the method of moments to solve numerically the matrix equation derived for the physical problem consisting in a finite number of anode wires between two cathode planes. Preliminary results show the capability of the algorithm to compute the edge effects which must be taken into account in the design of the detectors.

articleTitle: Mapping of installed optical cables on electric energy transmission lines in Brazil and possible new applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A great number of optical cable has been installed on electric energy transmission lines in Brazil. This work has been done by power utilities and telecommunication companies, which are, in general, state owned companies. However most of this work has been done independently. However, it became necessary to agglutinate this information. Cepel, the Brazilian Electric Energy Research Center, decided to compile all information related to the installation and use of optical cable on transmission lines (OCTL) in Brazil. We believe this work will help companies to link all the existing and planned systems, and to improve their connections and compatibility. The authors show tables and graphs with updated information.
