They also discuss how these systems can be used to monitor the energy transmission lines in a remote way to improve the system performance.

articleTitle: A finite element analysis of a radiating slot in guiding structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new method is proposed for the analysis of a transverse radiating slot coupled to a non-homogeneous guiding structure. Using the finite element method (FEM), arbitrarily complex cross-section guiding structures can be characterized and then, by means of an application of the reciprocity theorem, coupled to the slot. This approach overcomes the restrictions of previous methods, based on an application of method of moments (MoM), requiring the knowledge of the guiding structure Green's function. Further refinement of the computed radiated field is obtained by taking into account also the contribution arising from the diffraction at the edge of the perfectly conducting surface (of the rectangular waveguide walls) in which the slot resides.

articleTitle: Cylindrical rectangular microstrip antennas using slot coupling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Full wave spectral domain approach together with the reciprocity theorem are used to analyze a slot coupled cylindrical rectangular microstrip antenna. The slot is excited by either an open circuited stripline or an open circuited microstripline. The fields excited by the antenna patch surface current and the slot equivalent magnetic current for a multiple dielectric substrates coated cylinder are rigorously formulated using the spectral domain Green's functions. Numerical results for the input impedance and far-field pattern are presented. It is found that the input impedance is significantly affected by the cylinder size.

articleTitle: An optimum matching circuit for SAW filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents a lossless matching circuit for SAW filters that is two-fold optimum: it minimises the overall filter losses; and it provides a temperature behaviour without tilting either in amplitude or in phase. A theoretical justification for its use is presented and some measurement results illustrating these performance are shown. Also one procedure for tuning is described.

articleTitle: Unified dispersion model for a composite substrate shielded parallel coupled microstrip line using SLR technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A unified dispersion model for coupled microstrip line on the composite substrate with a top shield is presented by using the single layer reduction (SLR) technique and Kirschning-Jansen (1984) dispersion model for even-odd modes. Results have been compared against the results of Krage and Haddad (1972) within 3% deviation for three couplers. The present model is suitable for MIC and MMIC CAD application.

articleTitle: Recent developments in finite element analysis of optical and microwave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper summarizes and illustrates some of the current forms of using the finite element method in the analysis of microwave and optical structures. Modal and propagation methods are reviewed. An accurate and efficient method for the vectorial modal analysis of waveguides which also permits the treatment of open waveguides including leakage is described and illustrated with examples of complex modes in microwaves and a leaky ARROW structure in optics. The use of finite elements in propagation methods is also briefly described and illustrated.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of optical filters consisting of dielectric grating waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The propagation characteristics of dielectric grating waveguides are analyzed, using a rigorous modal theory. It is shown that the structures behave like transmission or reflection filters within a small range of some given parameters. Approximate expressions are also presented for the prediction of their characteristics and they are valuable for the design of these structures. It is also shown that the linewidths at the frequencies of maximum reflection or transmission may be conveniently adjusted by varying the design parameters. Finally, a discussion is presented on how to use these filters in some optical devices.

articleTitle: Coupling single-mode fiber to uniform and symmetrically tapered thin-film waveguide structures using gadolinium gallium garnet
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The need for high efficiency components has grown significantly due to the expanding role of fiber optic communications for various applications. Integrated optics is in a state of metamorphosis and there are many problems awaiting solutions. One of the main problems being the lack of a simple and efficient method of coupling single-mode fibers to thin-film devices for integrated optics. Optical coupling between a single-mode fiber and a uniform and tapered thin-film waveguide is theoretically modeled and analyzed. The novel tapered structure presented is shown to produce a perfect match for power transfer.

articleTitle: 550 /spl Aring/ tunable InGaAsP/InP MQW grating-assisted vertical wavelength-selective filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: It is reported, for the first time, a tunable grating-assisted vertical wavelength-selective filter based on InGaAsP/InP MQW. The filter presents a tunability range of 550 /spl Aring/ at 6.0 V, an optical and electrical bandwidth of 45 /spl Aring/ and 1.5 GHz, respectively. For unitary coupling efficiency the length is only 2.55 mm with 7.24 dB intrinsic loss.

articleTitle: Comparison between radiometrically measured and predicted attenuation at 23.8 and 31.4 GHz in temperate climate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The atmospheric attenuation in the absence of liquid water, both rain and clouds, is considered as a relevant parameter for the design of low availability satellite communication systems. The absorption due to oxygen and water vapour is derived from experimental radiometric measurements, carried out for one year in Roma, Italy, and calculated with the ITU-R algorithm, based on climatic surface data. The comparison shows that clear sky attenuation, mostly due to water vapour, can be accurately estimated by simplified models, the corresponding discrepancy with the measured "truth reference" being, however, dependent upon the degree of air humidity. The resultant indications are of relevance for the design of commercial systems, especially in those climates, such as the tropics, where the vapour density is usually higher with respect to temperate zones.

articleTitle: 24-channel synchronous parallel optical fiber interconnection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The article describes the complete experimental demonstration of an optoelectronic parallel interconnection spanning 24 parallel channels comprising three units of hermetically packaged monolithic 8-element laser array, integrated 8-element fiber optical ribbon, and monolithic 8-element photodetector array, and the corresponding 24-channel electronic circuitry for drive and reception. The experimental system has a 300 m fiber length per channel. All channels are totally independent both electrically and optically. The measured optical crosstalk (XTK) is <-40 dB, and the thermal XTK is <-30 dB. The total skew is less than 5 ns; and the BER is <10/sup -14/. Successful installation of the optical multichannel interconnection in a digital switching (Tropico RA) system demonstrated error-free operation and no degradation in performance, compared to the present (/spl ap/10 m cable length) standard electrical interconnection.

articleTitle: Assessment of the influence of radiowaves propagation conditions on the operation of the high-frequency direction finding positioning system in the Antarctic conditions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: There are significant difficulties in air traffic control during the radar operation in the Antarctic. The cost of radar installations is high, and a large number of radars is needed for long routes (about 1000 km or more). To solve this problem, the construction of a direction finding positioning system (DFPS) is needed. The results of the processing of the experimental data and zones of the DFPS operation for different radiowave propagation conditions are given.

articleTitle: Estimation of the parameters of a rain cell model from attenuation measurements in converging terrestrial links
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A rain cell model is used to derive expressions for the attenuation in six converging links (operating at 15 GHz and 18 GHz) and the measured rainfall rate at their nodal point. These expressions are adjusted to the experimental data to estimate the parameters of the model and to provide information on the structure and dynamics of rain cells in tropical regions.

articleTitle: An accurate six-port microstrip reflectometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper describes the properties of a novel 8-port coupler which has been assembled out of three 4-port interdigitated couplers. The procedures used in the design of this coupler, as well as in the derivation of its essential parameters are demonstrated. The scattering matrix of the proposed coupler is derived by using the signal flow graph (SFG) technique. The 8-port coupler has been modified with proper terminations in order to produce a working six-port reflectometer. Detailed SFG analysis of this reflectometer reveals that it is inherently of a broad-band character. This reflectometer has been fabricated, calibrated and tested at the X band.

articleTitle: An integrated optical technology based on sol-gel glasses on silicon: the NODES project
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The European collaboration project, NODES, aims to establish the basis of a new material and fabrication technology for low-cost mass production of multi-functional integrated optic components, based on spin-on sol-gel glass on silicon. We are developing materials using sol-gel silica as a host matrix, and semiconductor and rare-earth dopants for nonlinear and optical gain functions respectively, for demonstrator switching and amplifying devices. The paper describes the methods used, and the results obtained, in the project as a whole.

articleTitle: On the generalised loaded-line phase shifter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The loaded-line configuration for digital phase shifters is considered for the general situation of different switching admittances. Simple closed-form expressions are derived for the usual case of admittances separated by a quarter-wavelength transmission line.

articleTitle: Measurement method of permittivity variations of loss liquid materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new approach to permittivity measurement applied to loss materials is examined. The method proposed is based on the utilisation of a waveguide bridge and the precise knowledge of the field. Liquid dielectrics are the main focus, but the approach applies to other materials. A finite element method is used near to the dielectric. A modal decomposition is employed far from the source. Experimental measurement acquisition reveals a standing wave curve between two samples. The experimental results are compared to the theoretical curves.

articleTitle: Efficient coupling of a graded index glass guide to a polymer guide by means of a tapered transition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A new four layer tapered coupler (FLTC) has been studied and tested, able to transfer light efficiently from a monomode fiber to a polymer film guide by means of an auxiliary graded index glass waveguide. A simple theory has been developed to calculate the maximum efficiency of these structures. Experiments have been performed at /spl lambda/=1.321 /spl mu/m on several FLTC samples, containing K/sup +/-Na/sup +/ ion-exchanged glass waveguides and spin coated poly-3BCMU films. Insertion losses in the range 3-6.5 dB have been measured, depending on the taper configuration. The agreement between theoretical and experimental data is good, provided that a suitable ripple of the taper profile is assumed.

articleTitle: The capacity of a CDMA wireless system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Code division multiple access is a technique in which several users access a common medium, by modulating their symbols with designed spreading sequences. This article describes and analyzes a model for the discrete-input continuous-output Gaussian multiple access channel, that uses spread spectrum techniques. The relationship between the capacity of such system and the associated probability of error is also presented.

articleTitle: Trains of bright solitons in birefringent fibres
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A computational study of the propagation stability of trains of bright solitons in monomode birefringent fibres is presented for the first time. Several decisive operational conditions are established. These may be used to optimise the propagation distance and bit rate capacity of an optical-soliton-based transmission system.

articleTitle: An adaptive linearizer using feedback and dynamic biasing techniques for SSPAs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A novel adaptive envelope feedback linearizer using a dynamic gate bias for gain stabilization has been developed and validated using PIP MDS software. A two-tone test at around 14 GHz for a 25 dBm solid state power amplifier (SSPA) shows an average in-band intermodulation product below -35 dBc up to saturation. This linearity enhancement is accompanied by only a 10% increase (in average) in the power-added efficiency from 35% to 45%.

articleTitle: Capacity comparison between the GSM mobile radio system and a CDMA-based one
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Performance comparisons between the European mobile radio system, GSM, and one with a DS-CDMA access technique, based on the IS 95 Standard, are carried out in terms of link budgets and capacity evaluations. The same working conditions and the same cellular coverage have been adopted with the aim of performing significant comparison between the two systems. In particular, the performance has been evaluated in outdoor urban and quasi-open rural environments, under the hypothesis that the mobile terminals transmit with the same mean power.

articleTitle: Trends in mobile communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Some current developments of digital mobile systems are discussed including new coding techniques, channel modelling and simulation programs. Progress in high GHz-techniques and smart hardware development is illustrated. International exposure limits for biological interaction are summarized.

articleTitle: Eigenmodes in open coaxial cylindrical resonators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The electrodynamical properties of open coaxial cylindrical resonators using a partially-conical inner rod are examined on the basis of a resonance criterion for the eigenmodes. Owing to the spectral rearrangement arising from the presence of a coaxial insert, it turns out possible to isolate the desired operating mode from its neighboring competitors. The modelling of an especially designed cavity demonstrates that the corresponding TE-mode spectrum is markedly diluted in the 5-10 GHz range. The coaxial structure with a conical inner rod, is shown to be highly selective, and can find useful applications in high-power gyrotrons and frequency-tunable resonators.

articleTitle: Application of band-limited functions to the analysis of axially symmetric reflectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A band-limited set of basis functions is employed, in a 3-D situation, to reduce the spatial-sample count associated with the method of moments (MoM) procedure. Results obtained from modelling axially symmetric reflectors, using variable spatial sample counts, are compared with ones derived from other classes of basis functions. The comparison evidences a superior computational performance (CPU time and memory requirements) of the proposed scheme in this context.

articleTitle: Characterization of directional coupler-based optical guided-wave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The accurate characterization of directional coupler-based photonic devices is presented using the coupled mode and the least squares boundary residual approaches along with the finite element method. Results are obtained showing the power transfer ratio between such coupled waveguides, and compare favourably with those of published data.

articleTitle: A new principle of the joint spatial adaptive interference cancellation and signal demodulation in communication receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The paper concerns the situation in radio communications when almost the full information about the manipulated desired signal is available, excluding only the manipulating sequence itself. The method proposed is to solve the least squares problem where the reference signal is expressed as a linear combination of the known signals with unknown coefficients, which are adaptively tuned simultaneously with the spatial filtering weights. The method may be used for intersymbol interference cancellation in multipath channels as well as in the case of the noisy interference.

articleTitle: A modified method of lines for open and shielded structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A modified approach to the method of lines (MMOL) is used to analyze shielded and open planar microwave structures. This method is based on transformation functions to reduce the number of lines while maintaining the so-called edge condition. An extensive study on the choice of these transformation functions is performed in this paper. Numerical results show the potential gain both in computational efficiency and accuracy as compared to the original MOL.

articleTitle: Microwave approach to a class of highly irregular fiber optics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Variably coupled-mode theory developed decades ago in the microwave art is rediscovered to be a powerful mathematical tool in dealing with highly irregular fiber optics, whose analytic solution would have been extremely difficult to obtain if adopting a regular optical method. Examples treated in this presentation are the author's new invention of a set of fiber-optic analogues of bulk-optic wave plates. Experimental data exactly confirm theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Flexible IF processors for future communications payloads
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents an IF processor built around a "brick-wall" named BIFFAC, using SAW filters, ASICs and FPGAs on just one multilayer printed circuit board. This BIFFAC provides the input multiplexing of a 21 MHz bandwidth to up to 4 outputs having independently programmable sub-bands, in steps of 3 MHz, and gains of up to 31 dB by 1 dB steps. A breadboard of one IF processor using 3 BIFFACs has been built, emulating a flexible payload, interconnecting two up-links to two down links. Measurements results and hardware photos are presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter radio astronomical research: acousto-optic spectrometer device and measurement uncertainties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: To overcome the limits imposed by acoustic attenuation and velocity, a low cost acousto-electro-optic interaction configuration with high channel number possibilities is proposed. From the turbulence and temperature effects on the measurement uncertainties, the authors establish the relative importance of those two parameters for radio astronomical observations at millimeter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Characteristic propagation of the shielded high-Tc superconducting microstrip lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The rigorous method in the spectral domain of the transverse transmission line (TTL) is used in the analysis of shielded microstrip lines considering the superconductor strip for the first time. Previously, the open superconductor microstrip line was considered by the authors and now they present the effects of the superconducting material in the strip in a shielded planar structure. The superconductor effect is included in this procedure using the complex resistive boundary conditions model. The surface impedance is related to the complex conductivity of the material that is calculated from an enhanced two-fluid model. Numerical results are presented for the propagation constant and normalized phase velocity as a function of the frequency and of the thickness of the strip for shielded superconductor microstrip lines and substrate with losses.

articleTitle: Laser diode module for multi gigabit/sec lightwave transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A bandwidth of over 6 GHz has been obtained in a InGaAsP-InP DCPBH laser diode module. A mesa structure was introduced to reduce the parasitic capacitance and leakage current. The microwave design and simulation show the influence of the thermoelectric cooler and the lead inductance. This LD module can be applied to 2.488 Gb/s optical transmission (SDH).

articleTitle: Multi-chip modules for digital, analog and optical applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: MCMs offer an effective approach for the implementation of mixed signal and electro-optical circuits. The paper describes MCM types (-L, -C, and -D), discuss cost-performance trade-off, and the design methodology for analog and digital MCM circuits. Significant performance improvements attributed to the MCM embodiment were observed in the digital and microwave circuits of a MCM-D direct digital synthesis (DDS)/single sideband (SSB) upconverter when the number of interfaces and associated parasitic effects were reduced.

articleTitle: Frequency-dependent FDTD method applied to optically-controlled coupled-dielectric-waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The finite-difference time domain (FDTD) method for dispersive media is applied to the study of the electromagnetic wave propagation in optically-controlled coupled-dielectric-waveguides. The optical control is achieved by means of light incidence on semiconductor layers deposited onto the waveguides. The effects produced by the induced plasma in the semiconductor are analyzed through the dispersion characteristic of the waveguide structure.

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of a through hole via with time dependent skin effect model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents a transient simulation of a through hole via connecting transmission lines on both sides of a printed circuit board. The via is modeled by a lumped RLC equivalent circuit that takes into account the skin effect in the cylindrical conductor. In the analysis of the transmission line part, a new skin effect model accounting for the time dependent losses is included. A mathematical interface is established between discrete time domain solutions and a lumped element RLC circuit. Numerical results show reasonable response due to the through hole via.

articleTitle: Optical intensity modulator based on electrically induced periodic structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An optical intensity modulator based on electrically induced periodic structure in a pn diode is reported. The interaction of the microwave electric field and the pn junction carriers results in a periodic structure which modulates the light intensity. Simulations have shown that a device 370 /spl mu/m long, operating at -4.0 V, presents a bandwidth of 6.5 GHz at a modulation depth of 0.5 and an optical intrinsic loss of only 0.33 dB.

articleTitle: The use of automatic differentiation in advanced non-linear modelling of microwave active devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We describe the use of a novel, flexible and highly modular simulation environment called Sframe, in microwave device modelling and circuit simulation. The software architecture of Sframe is based on object orientation, automatic differentiation and the use of off-the-shelf numerical codes. We present the first tests with the implementation of an advanced nonlinear GaAs FET model in Sframe. This general purpose model, introduces novel solutions, particularly with respect to the modelling of the gate charge, gate capacitances and the RF dispersion of the transconductance and output conductance. The use of automatic differentiation techniques and the modularity of Sframe, lead to very compact model codes, simplifies the implementation process and eliminates many common sources of error. DC and small-signal AC simulation tests have been successfully carried out and the results are shown for the case of a 0.5 /spl mu/m GaAs MESFET.

articleTitle: Comparison between ITU-T Recs G.826/spl times/G.821: a concrete case in Brazil
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between the limits of the ITU-T Recs G.826 and G.821 in a 5 GHz-32 QAM-155 Mbits/s (STM-1) radio system, to be implemented from Vitoria (ES) to Salvador (Brazil). This backbone is composed of 17 hops (with an average length of 54 km) near the coast, divided in four baseband sections. The results of this design is presented, comparing the G.821 criteria with the corresponding G.826 ones and it is shown that although there were some pessimist expectations to the compliance of the G.826 criteria, these limits are achieved without requiring very large infrastructure modification or hardware adaptations.

articleTitle: Patterning of poly-3BCMU nonlinear waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Experimental studies of the photobleaching technique is reported in the case of spin coated films of poly-3BCMU. This technique was utilized to fabricate tapered waveguides, gratings and waveguide lenses. The authors' results confirm the potential of photobleaching for polymer based nonlinear integrated optics.

articleTitle: Stationary measurement of the response time in reversible optical recording materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We report a steady-state continuous technique for the measurement of the response-time in reversible optical recording materials. This method is based on phase modulation and homodyne detection techniques and is particularly suited for fast materials. Experiment is carried out using an undoped semi-insulating GaAs crystal.

articleTitle: Radar magnetrons: international and Brazilian Air-Force scenarios
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Microwave high power technology would not be conceivable without the early development of the radar magnetron by H.A.H. Boot, J.T. Randall, and their associates in England in late 1939. It is pointed out that with an appropriate substitution of the conventional fixed frequency or mechanically tuned strapped anode structures for the coaxial anode structure coupled with a sophisticated tuning mechanism one can upgrade the dated Brazilian Air-Force radar systems. This retrofitting approach can be installed in the existing airborne and ground-based radar. It represents a low percentage of the total radar cost, about 10-15% of the original system cost. Therefore, an economical and attractive program can be accomplished by the civil and military government sectors working together towards common objectives.

articleTitle: Application of microwave techniques in agricultural research
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Microwave techniques, methods and instrumentation can be utilized to increase and improve efficiency of crop production and enhance crop quality. Some examples of successful applications of microwaves in agriculture are presented, and future prospects are discussed. The applications of microwave reflected waves for agricultural purposes discussed are related mainly to various applications of radar.

articleTitle: Interactive multimedia lessons for education
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The development of interactive multimedia modules for education presents a significant opportunity to modernize engineering, science and math curricula and improve the effectiveness of teaching and learning of these subjects. We review the various hardware and software components required to develop multimedia lessons and discuss the role of each component in the structure of the multimedia module. Several examples of multimedia products available from the CAEME Center are demonstrated. This includes the extensive electromagnetics software published in Volumes I and II of the CAEME books, the Calculus Castle, the Physics Museum; and interactive multimedia games such as "Tic-Tac-Toe" in calculus and "Frantic Physics", a space-invaders-type review game in physics. It is shown that although extensive resources and expertise are often needed to develop these modules, the technology is readily available and educators are encouraged to take advantage of these available opportunities to reform engineering, science, and math education.

articleTitle: Novel antennas for personal communications including biological effects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The electromagnetic interaction between handset-mounted antennas and the nearby biological tissue is a key consideration in modern personal communications. A thorough investigation of this antenna-tissue interaction using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulation approach is presented using detailed models of real-life antennas on a transceiver handset. Representative examples of external and internal antenna configurations are considered. Detailed models of the human head and hand are implemented to investigate the effects of the tissue location and physical model on the antenna performance. The specific absorption rate (SAR) in the tissue is examined for several different antenna/handset configurations. It is found that for a head and handset antenna separation of 2 cm, the SAR in the head has a peak value between 0.9 and 3.8 mW/g and an average value between 0.06 and 0.10 mW/g for 1 W of power delivered to the antenna. Additionally, the head and hand could absorb between 48 and 68% of the power delivered to the antenna.

articleTitle: Future trends of mobile and personal communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This tutorial paper provides an overview of the fundamental concepts used in cellular radio communications, and illustrates the likely evolution and growth of the personal communications field. This paper also summarizes some of the most popular wireless standards used throughout the world.

articleTitle: Issues in the modeling of fiber optic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1995 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Computer aided design (CAD) tools prepare for an expanded role in the design of fiber-optical systems for high-performance computing and communications systems. One crucial part of the design of CAD tools is the efficient modeling of the optoelectronic components and the accurate prediction of the optical pulse deterioration along the optical link. This paper discusses circuit- and system-level models issues for fiber-optic interconnects consisting of optical devices such as laser diodes, photoreceivers, optical fibers, and other optoelectronic devices.
